summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted due to worsening scabbing and bleeding from her left brachiobasilic AV fistula, found to have an aneurysm. She underwent a bovine jump graft revision to address the complication while preserving dialysis access. The procedure was successful, with no intraoperative complications. Postoperatively, she experienced mild nausea managed with antiemetics, and minor oozing from the incision was noted but resolved with dressing replacement. She remained hemodynamically stable, afebrile, and tolerated oral intake and ambulation. She was discharged home with home health services, with instructions for incision care, activity restrictions, and close monitoring for signs of infection or graft dysfunction. Follow-up was arranged with her surgical and dialysis teams.
